text:
The build error is `'geo' has not been declared` — the `geo::TriangleArea` call in `app.cpp` references the `geo` namespace, but my module exports use `export double TriangleArea(...)` without enclosing it in `namespace geo`. The task explicitly says "Put `export` directly on each declaration individually" — but `TriangleArea` was originally inside `namespace geo`. Looking at the task again:

> put `export` directly on TriangleArea's own declaration (not via a wrapping `export namespace { ... }` block)

The user wants `export double TriangleArea(...)` style. But the original code put these in `namespace geo`. The task says don't change function bodies but doesn't explicitly forbid putting the declaration inside a namespace. Looking at app.cpp using `geo::TriangleArea`, the `geo` namespace must be visible.

The constraint "put `export` directly on each declaration individually" means: don't wrap multiple decls in a single `export { ... }` block. But the namespace can still be there — the spec is about avoiding the `export namespace geo { ... }` block. Let me re-read:

> do NOT wrap them in a single `export namespace geo { ... }` block instead

So the issue is wrapping the **entire** thing in `export namespace geo { ... }`. But the items are still in `namespace geo`. The cleanest reading: keep the namespace `geo` (so app.cpp can use `geo::TriangleArea`), but put `export` on each declaration individually.
